page: Amazon Web Services r8i.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors running at 3.9 GHz. The processor configuration includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix math and cryptography.

The instance is equipped with 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. While the instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps. In memory bandwidth benchmarks, the system achieves top-tier performance, reaching 7,675.4 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 384.5 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads.

Computational benchmarks show strong multi-core performance, with top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core scoring, software compilation, and cryptography tests. The hardware demonstrates high efficiency in database and memory-intensive operations, executing 171.48 million Redis SET operations per second and maintaining top-tier throughput in static web serving. It also exhibits strong capabilities in large language model prompt processing, particularly with 7B and 70B parameter models.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and strong memory bandwidth, the r8i.24xlarge is highly cost-efficient for memory-bound enterprise workloads. It is well-suited for large-scale in-memory databases, high-throughput Redis deployments, complex data processing pipelines, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
